title: Safeguards and review of GIRO deductions
asked: MPs asked about safeguards against duplicate or erroneous GIRO deductions, due diligence on billing organisations, and whether MAS will require banks to let customers set limits on the number or total value of deductions per billing period.
asked_by: Ms Gho Sze Kee, Mr Shawn Loh and Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
response: Mr Alvin Tan said customers can already set transaction limits on GIRO payments, and banks conduct due diligence on billing organisations, including checking they are properly registered and not linked to sanctioned or criminal activities. He said bank checks may not always prevent errors or misuse, and MAS is working with the Association of Banks in Singapore and member banks to strengthen safeguards. The review will consider monthly limits on the value and number of transactions, enhanced transaction monitoring, and stronger due diligence on billing organisations. He also advised consumers to review their GIRO arrangements and set appropriate limits, and noted non-GIRO options such as standing instructions.

key_points.point: Customers can set transaction limits on their GIRO payments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Customers can set transaction limits on their GIRO payments.

key_points.point: Banks apply due diligence checks on GIRO billing organisations, including checking they are properly registered and not linked to sanctioned or criminal activities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: These include checking that they are properly registered businesses and are not linked to any sanctioned or other criminal activities.

key_points.point: Bank checks may not always prevent errors and potential misuse of GIRO.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: checks by banks may not always be able to prevent errors and potential misuse of GIRO

key_points.point: The review will consider monthly limits on the value and number of transactions, enhanced transaction monitoring, and due diligence on billing organisations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: The review will consider measures including enabling customers to set monthly limits on the value and number of transactions and enhancing transaction monitoring and due diligence on billing organisations.

key_points.point: Consumers are advised to review their GIRO arrangements and set appropriate transaction limits.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: We also advise consumers to review their current GIRO arrangements and to set appropriate transaction limits with their banks and financial institutions.

key_points.point: Some banks offer GIRO on-demand, where each deduction must be authorised individually.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: some of the banks have, for example, GIRO on-demand, where each deduction must be authorised individually before the bank processes the transaction.

key_points.point: MAS will work with banks and financial institutions to raise public awareness.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: MAS will work with the banks, as well as financial institutions to raise awareness and public awareness of these.

left_open: Whether mandatory pre-debit notifications will be part of the review.
The specific due diligence checks required when onboarding a corporate customer for GIRO billing.
Whether banks are required to have suspicious transaction alerts for multiple GIRO deductions in a short time span.
The timeline for completing the review.
supplementary: Supplementary questions asked about UK direct debit safeguards, the review timeline and public awareness, and monitoring for anomalous GIRO deduction patterns.
